podcast.body: The Winstons, an American soul group, recorded "Amen Brother" in 1969, which contains a seven-second drum bit by Gregory Coleman, known as the "Amen Break." This segment has become the "most sampled piece of music in the universe," reportedly used in nearly 6,200 songs according to whosample.com. "In 1969, an American solo group called The Wind Stins recorded a song called Amen Brother. It features a seven-second drum bit by Gregory Coleman."

podcast.body: This 1969 song is notable because its drum break makes it the second most sampled song, after James Brown's extensive catalog. The "Amen break" from this track is a fundamental building block in countless hip hop, jungle, drum and bass, and other electronic music productions. "The next closest competition is the Winston's, largely because of their 1969 song, Amen Brother."

podcast.body: The drum solo from this song is one of the most sampled and recognizable beats in hip hop history. Dr. Dre notably sampled and slowed this particular section for the N.W.A. song "Straight Outta Compton," and in the early 1990s in the UK, various musicians accelerated and chopped this same solo to create the Drum & Bass genre. "Se trata de la canción a Membroder de la banda de Winston's."
